text:
alex: Quick experiment notes — tried a lazy-defrag + batch-amortization approach to cut per-sequence workspace churn. Goal: reduce short-lived allocations that explode when batch size grows.

alex: baseline allocator stats from yesterday (peak GPU mem 78GB, app cap 80GB): free_slots=2148, frag_bytes=1.9GB, avg_seq_overhead=12KB, steady_batch=64

alex: patch toggles used: 
```
export RWLA_LAZY_DEFRAG=1
export RWLA_BATCH_AMORTIZE=1
./bin/serve --batch-max 256 --ws-min 64
```

sam: nice. what's amortization mean here? do you pool per-seq buffers across batches or just delay free? :thinking_face:

alex: both. We keep a small ring of 'leased' slots per device that can be reused across subsequent batches for the same kernel footprint. Only fully free when the ring exceeds a threshold or on low-pressure GC.

maria: ran profiler during a 4h load test. Observations: when batch grows from 64->192 we saved ~28% allocation churn, reduced calls to cuMemFree by ~45%, and kernel queue stalls dropped a bit. But tail latency jitter increased for some 1-2% of requests.

ryan: interesting — could jitter be due to background defrag work being run inline? are we running defrag on caller thread vs bg worker?

alex: current impl runs quick inline coalesces for same-size neighbors, and defers larger compaction tasks to a bg thread. But in heavy load the bg worker can't keep up and we start doing more inline work.

isha: how does this interact with KV cache? I worry leasing slots might hold on to KV shadow buffers and block evictions, causing memory pressure.

maria: saw that: KV shadow pages were pinned ~14% longer. But overall OOMs dropped in our stress runs. We still had a few OOMs when sequence length distribution spiked (many long-seq tails).

alex: repro steps I used (very short):
```
# run synthetic workload
python stress_clients.py --p50=20 --p95=128 --qps=1200 --duration=20m
# enable flags
RWLA_LAZY_DEFRAG=1 RWLA_BATCH_AMORTIZE=1 ./bin/serve --ws-min=64 --batch-max=256
```

sam: can you paste the small heapdump snippet from the allocator debug log? curious about fragmentation pattern.

alex: snippet: 
```
[allocator] live=72GB reserved=80GB free_chunks=192 largest_free=2.1GB overhead_seq=9.8KB leak_cand=3
[batch] active_batches=9 avg_elems=87 amort_ring=128 pinned_kv=34MB
```

ryan: kernel selection note: when we reuse buffers across kernels that change sequence lengths, some kernels fall back to alternate code path (non-tiled) and allocate temporary workspace. We should record kernel variant with the slot so reuse is only allowed for compatible kernel descriptors.

alex: good call. I didn't tag descriptors in the amort_ring, just size. that explains some of the temp allocs.

isha: policy Q: what threshold triggers full free? we should avoid holding >1.5x working set.

alex: current thresholds: lease_ring_size = max(64, batch_max/2), free_on_pressure_pct = 75%. We can tune.

maria: perf matrices: across three runs:
- baseline: p99 mem spikes 79.4GB, OOMs=3, avg latency=42ms
- lazy-defrag only: p99 mem spikes 77.8GB, OOMs=1, avg latency=45ms
- lazy+amortize: p99 mem spikes 74.9GB, OOMs=0, avg latency=47ms, but p99.9 latency had 2 regressions (1x ~900ms)

sam: tolerable trade if we can bound the high tail. maybe backpressure the amort_ring growth when tail latency crosses a threshold.

ryan: also measure kernel-switch penalty: cache a small header with kernel_id + seq_range. Reuse only when kernel_id matches; otherwise evict and do fresh alloc.

alex: I'll prototype tagging and a backpressure signal: if p99 latency > 200ms then cap amort_ring to 16 and trigger aggressive bg defrag.

devops-bot: deploy triggered by alex at 2026-03-18T14:23:02Z — canary on prod-rlw-2 (3 nodes)

isha: we should add KV-aware eviction: if pinned_kv > 10% of free, prefer freeing leased slots that shadow KV first.

maria: agree. Also add a debug trace for "slot_origin" in allocator logs so we can see if slots are reused for different kernels frequently.

alex: action list I propose:
1) tag amort_ring slots with kernel_desc (alex, this week)
2) implement latency-based ring cap/backpressure (alex + sam, this week)
3) KV-aware lease eviction policy (isha, next sprint)
4) add slot_origin tracing and a small analysis job to find cross-kernel reuse (maria, next week)
5) run 24h burn with synthetic dist and real traffic mixed (ryan, infra)

sam: +1. please add a short note in the perf board about expected p99.9 regression and mitigation steps.

alex: will do. uploading short patch in PR 7245 with an opt-in flag. need reviewers from kernel-selection and kv teams. cc @ryan @isha

maria: cool. happy to run the analysis once traces are in. :+1:

alex: TL;DR: lazy-defrag + amortized slot leasing cuts allocation churn and memory spikes, but we must tag slots by kernel and add latency-driven caps and KV-aware evictions to avoid p99 tail regressions and KV pressure.
